title: Who took what: joining three tables
instructions:
## The question

Produce the **2025-1** semester mark sheet: student **name**, course **title** and **mark**, for every enrolment in semester `'2025-1'`, sorted by name then title. Include enrolments whose mark is still NULL.

The database has three tables: **students** (id, name, programme, level, hometown), **courses** (code, title, credits, lecturer) and **enrolments** (student_id, course_code, semester, mark). Marks can be NULL when a result is not yet in. Use the Tables panel to peek at the data.

## Do this

Join `enrolments` to `students` (on the student id) and to `courses` (on the course code). Use table aliases to keep it readable:

```sql
SELECT s.name, c.title, e.mark
FROM enrolments e
JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id
JOIN ...
```

Then filter by semester and sort.

config.schema:
CREATE TABLE students (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  programme TEXT NOT NULL,
  level INTEGER NOT NULL,
  hometown TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE courses (
  code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  credits INTEGER NOT NULL,
  lecturer TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE enrolments (
  student_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES students(id),
  course_code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES courses(code),
  semester TEXT NOT NULL,
  mark INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY (student_id, course_code, semester)
);

hints: `JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id` links each enrolment to its student.
`JOIN courses c ON c.code = e.course_code` links it to the course.

checks.expectedQuery: SELECT s.name, c.title, e.mark FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.code = e.course_code WHERE e.semester = '2025-1' ORDER BY s.name, c.title

realityNote: In a production registry the same join runs over millions of enrolment rows; indexes on student_id and course_code are what keep it fast.
